**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Confluence space `SFCC` has 146 pages under a numbered "SFCC Migration" tree. Here's the distilled result for a React/frontend developer.

## Must-read (in priority order)

**Before touching code:**
1. [Technical Solution Design – PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) — the real architecture doc: integration boundary classes (Browser-direct/MRT-mediated/SFCC-cartridge/MuleSoft/Out-of-band), full multi-site session/basket model (7 sites, 6 regions, 11 locales — basket never crosses sites), SSR-vs-CSR pattern per page type, env-var security table, and a Didomi consent-gate table with several **still-TBC** purpose IDs (Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar, Measmerize, Vimeo, reCAPTCHA-EU/UK).
2. [1.5 Web Design (UX)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268075023) + [04.2 Design Tracker](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/258801666) — **hard build gate not in AGENTS.md**: only build to Signed-Off Figma frames. As of 2026-07-13, Homepage/PLP core grid/nav-footer/most PDP components/Payments-NotifyMe are signed off; **Cart, Search, Checkout, Account, Wishlist, Gift Cards, Returns, Store Locator, Z.immerse are still Draft/In Review** — check the tracker before building in those areas (saved to memory since it'll change).

**Setup & tooling:**
3. [Technical Environment Setup](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304906242) — but likely **stale**: it says `cp .env.sample .env` with no mention of the tiered `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` system or `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` your current `feature/env-switching` branch is building.
4. [Development Standards](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261750785) + [Component Override Strategy](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261881857) — **two direct conflicts with AGENTS.md**, see below.
5. [Branching Guide (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733) — adds detail AGENTS.md doesn't state: `develop` needs 2 approvals, `main` needs 2 (both squad leads), `release/**` needs 1 + branch restricted to squad leads.
6. [PWA CI/CD Pipeline](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305561601) + [SIT Quality Gates](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840754) — Lighthouse thresholds (Perf ≥80/A11y ≥90/BP ≥90), bundle limits (main.js<180kB/vendor.js<250kB/main.css<50kB).
7. [Claude Code CLI — Atlassian MCP Setup](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305004545) — needs `uv`, `direnv`, a personal Atlassian API token in local `.env`.

**Testing:** [AI-Assisted QA Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962) through Guide 4 — a six-stage Story→AC→Zephyr→Playwright→BrowserStack→Triage pipeline (including an autonomous defect-triage agent) that sits above what `.claude/rules/testing.md` describes and isn't referenced there at all.

## Setup checklist (as prescribed)

- **Access to request** (per [7.1a Tool Access Tracker](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/259686402)): your own row shows Jira/Confluence as "Requested" (not confirmed) and Figma as "View" only — worth confirming those are actually active, and whether View is enough or you need Figma Dev-mode.
- **Local machine**: Node 18/20/22/24, `npm ci` (installs Husky hooks), env file setup (see conflict above — confirm with your tech lead which method is current), ask Integration Lead for Commerce API + Contentful credentials, install Claude Code CLI.
- **MCP for Confluence/Jira**: `uv` + `direnv` installed, personal Atlassian API token, `direnv allow`, approve the MCP server on first prompt.
- **Contentful**: get invited as a Contentful user, generate your own CMA token, `npm run config:contentful`.
- **Program-level gaps still open** (per [7.1b](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268337165)/[7.1c](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530)): nearly every third-party credential (MuleSoft, Omneo, GiveX, Adyen, Global-e, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, reCAPTCHA, etc.) is still "Not yet requested"; BrowserStack account, `release/**` branch protection, and LHCI secrets aren't configured yet either — not blocking you personally, but worth knowing before assuming those integrations are testable end-to-end.

## Conflicts worth flagging to the team

1. **Icons** — Confluence says import directly from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`; AGENTS.md says the opposite (always use `overrides/app/components/icons`). Trust AGENTS.md — Confluence reads like the pre-override-pattern draft.
2. **New component location** — Confluence says new components go in `overrides/app/components/custom/<name>/`; the repo's actual convention (and the `/new-component` skill) skips the `custom/` layer entirely.

I saved the Confluence page map, these two conflicts, and the Figma sign-off snapshot to memory so future sessions don't need to re-crawl the space. Given the doc-integrity rule in AGENTS.md, these three points (icons, `custom/` folder, stale env-setup page) are probably worth a quick message to whoever owns Confluence updates rather than just living with the drift.
